summary: This note is a biography of Desmond Mason, an NBA player drafted 17th in 2000 by the Seattle SuperSonics out of Oklahoma State. It covers his Slam Dunk Contest results and his trades to the Milwaukee Bucks and New Orleans Hornets. It ends with his 2007 return to the Bucks.
one_line: Desmond Mason's NBA career: 2000 draft by Seattle, dunk contest results, trades to Milwaukee and New Orleans, and 2007 return to the Bucks.
key_facts: Desmond Mason was drafted out of Oklahoma State University by the Seattle SuperSonics with the 17th pick of the 2000 NBA draft.
In 2001, Desmond Mason became the first SuperSonics player in franchise history to win the NBA Slam Dunk Contest.
Desmond Mason finished in second place in the 2003 NBA Slam Dunk Contest behind Jason Richardson.
In 2003, Desmond Mason and Gary Payton were traded to the Milwaukee Bucks in exchange for Ray Allen and Ronald Murray.
On October 26, 2005, Desmond Mason was traded along with a first-round draft pick in the 2006 NBA draft to the New Orleans Hornets in exchange for Jamaal Magloire.
On July 23, 2007, Desmond Mason signed a contract with the Milwaukee Bucks after a two-season absence.
Desmond Mason was initially angry with Bucks general manager Larry Harris for trading him in 2005.
Desmond Mason said he was happy to be back in Milwaukee after rejoining the Bucks in 2007.
